why: MATLAB doc 'Object Arrays' and 'Concatenating Objects': indexing an object array with parentheses gives an array of its class (`k = k(1)`, `k = k(2:end)`), and concatenating objects of one class gives that class (`[k, Gizmo()]`, `[k; k]`), so `tidy(k)` dispatches to `Gizmo::tidy` (doc 'Method Invocation'), and `g = g(1)` keeps a `gadget`. Not so `k = k{1}` and `k = k.prop` (what a cell or a property holds is not stated: no class) nor `k = []` (a double): `tidy(k)` calls `tidy.m` there. (Review 2 finding 1, extended.)
